correctness.rationale: At the disease-free equilibrium, \(N^0=S^0+D^0\), so every infectious class has incidence derivative \(\beta\). With infected variables \((E,I_1,\ldots,I_n,C)\), only incidence into \(E\) belongs to the new-infection matrix. Progression \(E\to I_j\) and \(E\to C\) belongs to the transition matrix. The resulting \(FV^{-1}\) has rank one and spectral radius \(\frac{\beta}{\mu+\phi}[\alpha\sum_j\varphi_j/(\mu_j+\gamma_j+\mu)+(1-\alpha)\phi/(\mu+\delta_1+\gamma)]\). The exact two-strain witness gives published \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{src}}=9/10\), corrected \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pool}}=27/20\), and Jacobian eigenvalue \(-1+3\sqrt{15}/10>0\).

originality.rationale: The motivating article explicitly prints one shared exposed class but computes its multi-strain threshold by a strainwise maximum. Exact-DOI and statement-level searches found no source-specific correction. Earlier multi-strain papers do obtain maximum-of-strain thresholds, but their infection chains are separated by strain; that structure does not imply the threshold for the pooled exposed class in the 2026 model.
residual_risks: An unindexed correction could already amend the 2026 reproduction-number formula.
If the authors intended distinct exposed classes but printed one pooled exposed class, the biological model would need to be re-specified before applying this correction.
The endemic-equilibrium and optimal-control sections are outside the accepted claim.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The basic reproduction number is the central invasion threshold used by the article to classify the disease-free state and motivate control. The error is genuinely multi-strain: several subcritical return pathways can add through the shared exposed compartment and destabilize the disease-free state even though every published strainwise quantity is below one. The exact witness \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{src}}=9/10\) versus \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pool}}=27/20\) demonstrates a qualitative reversal rather than a minor numerical adjustment.
